arxiv-2010-14611.title: Hybrid Backpropagation Parallel Reservoir Networks
arxiv-2010-14611.creator: Matthew S. Evanusa, Snehesh Shrestha, Michelle Girvan, Cornelia Fermüller, Yiannis Aloimonos
arxiv-2010-14611.description: Abstract In many real-world applications, fully-differentiable RNNs such as LSTMs and GRUs have been widely deployed to solve time series learning tasks. These networks train via Backpropagation Through Time, which can work well in practice but involves a biologically unrealistic unrolling of the network in time for gradient updates, are computationally expensive, and can be hard to tune.

arxiv-2012-01233.title: Investigating two super-resolution methods for downscaling precipitation: ESRGAN and CAR
arxiv-2012-01233.creator: Campbell D. Watson, Chulin Wang, Timothy Lynar, Komminist Weldemariam
arxiv-2012-01233.description: Abstract In an effort to provide optimal inputs to downstream modeling systems (e.g., a hydrodynamics model that simulates the water circulation of a lake), we hereby strive to enhance resolution of precipitation fields from a weather model by up to 9x.

arxiv-2208-14852.title: Improving Operational Efficiency In EV Ridepooling Fleets By Predictive Exploitation of Idle Times
arxiv-2208-14852.creator: Jesper C. Provoost, Andreas Kamilaris, Gyözö Gidófalvi, Geert J. Heijenk, and Luc J.J. Wismans
arxiv-2208-14852.description: Abstract In ridepooling systems which are operated with an electric fleet, charging is an essential but complex decision-making process. Most contemporary electric vehicle (EV) taxi services require drivers to make egoistic decisions on where, when and how long to charge, leading to decentralized ad-hoc charging strategies.

arxiv-2209-02384.title: Data Centred Intelligent Geosciences: Research Agenda and Opportunities Position Paper Thanks: This work is funded by the project ADAGEO, IEA CNRS collaboration with Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte https://adageo.github.io .
arxiv-2209-02384.creator: Aderson Farias do Nascimento, Martin A. Musicante, Umberto Souza da Costa, Bruno M. Carvalho, Marcus Alexandre Nunes, Genoveva Vargas-Solar
arxiv-2209-02384.description: Abstract This paper describes and discusses our vision to develop and reason about best practices and novel ways of curating data-centric geosciences knowledge (data, experiments, models, methods, conclusions, and interpretations). This knowledge is produced from applying statistical modelling, Machine Learning, and modern data analytics methods on geo-data collections.

arxiv-2301-08646.title: The Gauge issue and the Hamiltonian theory of cosmological perturbations Thanks: Presented at POTOR8
arxiv-2301-08646.creator: Alice Boldrin
arxiv-2301-08646.description: Abstract We present a general formalism for the Hamiltonian description of perturbation theory around any spatially homogeneous spacetime. We employ and refine the Dirac method for constrained systems, which is very well-suited to cosmological perturbations. This approach includes a discussion of the gauge-invariant dynamics of perturbations as well as an analysis of gauge transformations, gauge-fixing, partial gauge-fixing and spacetime reconstruction.

arxiv-2306-06980.title: A CO Funnel in the Galactic Centre: Molecular Counterpart of the Northern Galactic Chimney?
arxiv-2306-06980.creator: V. S. Veena, D. Riquelme, W.-J. Kim, K. M. Menten, P. Schilke, M. C. Sormani, W. E. Banda-Barragán, F. Wyrowski, G. A. Fuller, A. Cheema
arxiv-2306-06980.description: Abstract We report the discovery of a velocity coherent, funnel shaped 13 CO emission feature in the Galactic centre (GC) using data from the SEDIGISM survey. The molecular cloud appears as a low velocity structure (V LSR {}_{\textrm{LSR}} =[–3.5, + + 3.5] km s -1 ) with an angular extent of 0.95 ∘ × 1 ∘ 0.

arxiv-2309-00804.title: The Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Operator on Discrete Weighted Morrey Spaces 0 0 footnotetext: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification . 46B45, 42B35, 42B25. Key words and phrases. weight, discrete Morrey space, discrete Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, discrete Calderón-Zygmund decomposition. This pr
arxiv-2309-00804.creator: Xuebing Hao, Shuai Yang, Baode Li
arxiv-2309-00804.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we introduce a discrete version of weighted Morrey spaces, and discuss the inclusion relations of these spaces. In addition, we obtain the boundedness of discrete weighted Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators on discrete weighted Lebesgue spaces by establishing a discrete Calderón-Zygmund decomposition for weighted l^{1} -sequences.

arxiv-2402-03214.title: Organic or Diffused: Can We Distinguish Human Art from AI-generated Images? Conference: Proceedings of the 2024 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security; October 14–18, 2024; Salt Lake City, UT, USA. Proceedings of the 2024 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Se
arxiv-2402-03214.creator: Anna Yoo Jeong Ha, Josephine Passananti, Ronik Bhaskar, Shawn Shan, Reid Southen, Haitao Zheng, Ben Y. Zhao
arxiv-2402-03214.description: Abstract . The advent of generative AI images has completely disrupted the art world. Distinguishing AI generated images from human art is a challenging problem whose impact is growing over time. A failure to address this problem allows bad actors to defraud individuals paying a premium for human art and companies whose stated policies forbid AI imagery.

arxiv-2406-12159.title: Exploring the Impact of a Transformer’s Latent Space Geometry on Downstream Task Performance
arxiv-2406-12159.creator: Anna C. Marbut, John W. Chandler, Travis J. Wheeler
arxiv-2406-12159.description: Abstract It is generally thought that transformer-based large language models benefit from pre-training by learning generic linguistic knowledge that can be focused on a specific task during fine-tuning. However, we propose that much of the benefit from pre-training may be captured by geometric characteristics of the latent space representations, divorced from any specific linguistic knowledge.

arxiv-2410-01121.title: Synchrotron break frequencies of mildly-to-highly relativistic outflows observed off-axis
arxiv-2410-01121.creator: Gilad Sadeh
arxiv-2410-01121.description: Abstract We consider the synchrotron spectrum produced by mildly-to-highly relativistic collisionless shocks. Simple analytic formulae are derived for the break frequencies (peak frequency, self-absorption frequency, synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling frequencies) of the emission produced by post-shock plasma elements propagating at an angle θ e \theta_{e} relative to the observer’s line of sight.

arxiv-2411-10838.title: Anisotropy in Pantheon+ supernovae
arxiv-2411-10838.creator: Animesh Sah, Mohamed Rameez, Subir Sarkar, ChristosTsagas
arxiv-2411-10838.description: Abstract We employ Maximum Likelihood Estimators to examine the Pantheon+ catalogue of Type Ia supernovae for large scale anisotropies in the expansion rate of the Universe. The analyses are carried out in the heliocentric frame, the CMB frame, as well as the Local Group frame. In all frames, the Hubble expansion rate in the redshift range 0.

arxiv-2503-07993.title: LLM-Powered Knowledge Graphs for Enterprise Intelligence and Analytics PubID: pubid: 979-8-3315-2480-7/25/$31.00 ©2025 IEEE
arxiv-2503-07993.creator: 1 st Rajeev Kumar, 2 nd Kumar Ishan, 3 rd Harishankar Kumar, 4 th Abhinandan Singla
arxiv-2503-07993.description: Abstract Disconnected data silos within enterprises obstruct the extraction of actionable insights, diminishing efficiency in areas such as product development, client engagement, meeting preparation, and analytics-driven decision-making. This paper introduces a framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to unify various data sources into a comprehensive, activity-centric knowledge graph.

arxiv-2510-21041.title: Gaussian Processes for Inferring Parton Distributions
arxiv-2510-21041.creator: Yamil Cahuana Medrano, Hervé Dutrieux, Joseph Karpie, Kostas Orginos, Savvas Zafeiropoulos, (on behalf of the HadStruc Collaboration)
arxiv-2510-21041.description: Abstract The extraction of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from experimental or lattice QCD data is an ill-posed inverse problem, where regularization strongly impacts both systematic uncertainties and the reliability of the results. We study a framework based on Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to reconstruct PDFs from lattice QCD matrix elements.

pmc-10607328.title: Mitigating Age-Related Ovarian Dysfunction with the Anti-Inflammatory Agent MIT-001
pmc-10607328.creator: Min-Hee Kang, Yu Jin Kim, Min Jeong Cho, JuYi Jang, Yun Dong Koo, Soon Ha Kim, Jae Ho Lee, Alfonso Gutiérrez-Adán
pmc-10607328.description: Ovarian aging is a major obstacle in assisted reproductive medicine because it leads to ovarian dysfunction in women of advanced age. Currently, there are no effective treatments to cure age-related ovarian dysfunction. In this study, we investigated the effect of MIT-001 on the function of aged ovaries. Young and old mice were utilized in this study.

pmc-11297276.title: Synergistic effects of COVID-19 pandemic and sedentary lifestyles on obesity rates among South Korean adults
pmc-11297276.creator: Wonseok Jeong, Wankyo Chung
pmc-11297276.description: Since March 2020, South Korea has implemented social distancing measures to reduce the spread of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19). These policies resulted in significant changes in the lifestyle of Korean adults, including spending more time indoors and experiencing increased sedentary time during the pandemic.

pmc-11460715.title: Longitudinal single-subject neuroimaging study reveals effects of daily environmental, physiological, and lifestyle factors on functional brain connectivity
pmc-11460715.creator: Ana María Triana, Juha Salmi, Nicholas Mark Edward Alexander Hayward, Jari Saramäki, Enrico Glerean, Kris Dickson, Ph.D., Kris Dickson, Ph.D., Kris Dickson, Ph.D., Kris Dickson, Ph.D., Christian Schnell, PhD, Christian Schnell, PhD, Christian Schnell, PhD
pmc-11460715.description: Our behavior and mental states are constantly shaped by our environment and experiences. However, little is known about the response of brain functional connectivity to environmental, physiological, and behavioral changes on different timescales, from days to months. This gives rise to an urgent need for longitudinal studies that collect high-frequency data.

pmc-11469161.title: Practical Aspects of Using Large Language Models to Screen Abstracts for Cardiovascular Drug Development: Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11469161.creator: Jay G Ronquillo, Jamie Ye, Donal Gorman, Adina R Lemeshow, Stephen J Watt, Christian Lovis
pmc-11469161.description: Cardiovascular drug development requires synthesizing relevant literature about indications, mechanisms, biomarkers, and outcomes. This short study investigates the performance, cost, and prompt engineering trade-offs of 3 large language models accelerating the literature screening process for cardiovascular drug development applications. Introduction Cardiovascular drug development requires synthesizing information about indications, mechanisms, biomarkers, and outcomes [1,2].

pmc-11675225.title: W-Class States—Identification and Quantification of Bell-CHSH Inequalities’ Violation
pmc-11675225.creator: Joanna K Kalaga, Wiesław Leoński, Jan Peřina, Sabre Kais, Dominik Szczęśniak
pmc-11675225.description: We discuss a family of W-class states describing three-qubit systems. For such systems, we analyze the relations between the entanglement measures and the nonlocality parameter for a two-mode mixed state related to the two-qubit subsystem. We find the conditions determining the boundary values of the negativity, parameterized by concurrence, for violating the Bell-CHSH inequality.

pmc-12386542.title: 25-Hydroxycholesterol Induces Intrinsic Apoptosis via Mitochondrial Pathway in BE(2)-C Human Neuroblastoma Cells
pmc-12386542.creator: Jaesung Kim, Koanhoi Kim, Dongha Park, Seong-Kug Eo, Bo-Ae Lee, Yonghae Son, Alfonso Baldi
pmc-12386542.description: An oxysterol, 25-Hydroxycholesterol (25OHChol), is produced through cholesterol oxidation and is involved in various cellular processes, including apoptosis. However, the precise mechanisms underlying 25OHChol-induced apoptosis in neuroblastoma cells remain unclear. The aim of this study was to elucidate the detailed molecular mechanisms by which 25OHChol induces apoptosis in human neuroblastoma cells.

pmc-12694353.title: DAF-YOLO: Detection of Unsafe Behaviors on Construction Sites
pmc-12694353.creator: Qi Xu, Xiang Cheng, Xiaoxiong Zhou, Xuejun Jia, Xiaoxiao Wang, Zhihan Shi, Shanshan Huang, Guangming Zhang
pmc-12694353.description: Construction sites are complex environments, and unsafe behaviors by workers, such as not wearing safety helmets or reflective vests, can easily lead to accidents. When using target detection technology to detect unsafe behaviors, the results are often unsatisfactory due to the complexity of the background and the small size of the targets.
